bib.title: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines

read.skipped: Figures 1-12 are images and were not viewed; only text and captions read. Annotation guideline pages (Figs 8-12) read as extracted text.

question: How verifiable (comprehensively and accurately cited) are the responses of popular commercial generative search engines?
hypothesis: Implied: existing generative search engines produce fluent, useful-looking answers whose citations often do not support them; the authors also hypothesise that the inverse correlation of citation precision with perceived utility arises because systems copy or closely paraphrase cited pages.
contributions: Define the citation recall and citation precision evaluation metrics (plus citation F1).
Human evaluation of four commercial generative search engines: responses are fluent and appear useful but frequently contain unsupported statements and inaccurate citations.
Observe that perceived utility is inversely correlated with citation precision, and hypothesise this comes from copying or closely paraphrasing cited webpages.

method.summary: Human audit of Bing Chat, NeevaAI, perplexity.ai and YouChat on 1450 queries each, drawn from 12 query distributions. Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators rate fluency and perceived utility, mark verification-worthy sentences, and judge whether each citation supports its sentence (AIS framework), from which citation recall, precision and F1 are computed.
method.task: Auditing verifiability (citation recall and precision) of generative search engine responses

models.name: Bing Chat

inference.samples: One response per query per system: the system's first complete (single-turn) response, scraped late February to late March 2023. Each query-response pair annotated once; 250 pairs annotated three times for agreement.
inference.prompting: No prompting of the evaluated systems beyond the raw query; ELI5 titles stripped of prefix, WikiHow titles turned into keyword queries.
inference.retrieval: Not controllable: commercial systems' own retrieval; the cited webpages were judged as given.

parameters.citation_set: C_i = citations occurring in sentence s_i

other.not_evaluated: ChatGPT and Bard, because they gave no in-line citations as of March 2023

metrics.name: Fluency
metrics.definition: Agreement on a five-point Likert scale with 'The response is fluent and cohesive'

metrics.name: Perceived utility
metrics.definition: Agreement on a five-point Likert scale with 'The response is a helpful and informative answer to the query'

metrics.name: Citation recall
metrics.definition: Proportion of verification-worthy statements fully supported by their associated citations (AIS: a generic hearer would affirm 'According to cited webpages Ci, si')

metrics.name: Citation precision
metrics.definition: (Tfs + Tps)/N where Tfs = citations fully supporting their statement, Tps = partially supporting citations whose statement is fully supported by the union of its citations and by no single citation, N = total citations

metrics.name: Citation F1
metrics.definition: Harmonic mean of citation precision and recall

metrics.name: BLEU / BERTScore (F1)
metrics.definition: Similarity between each generated statement and annotator-provided minimal evidence sentences from the cited page; maximum over associated citations

baselines: No baseline; the four systems are compared with each other.
eval.protocol: Human evaluation on Amazon Mechanical Turk with three steps (fluency/utility; filter non-verification-worthy sentences; per-citation full/partial/no support plus union judgment). 34 annotators passed a qualification study (read guidelines, evaluate five query-response pairs, personalised feedback). Pay $1.00 per pair with citations, $0.38 without ($15.00 per hour, by conservative time estimates); about four minutes per pair. Agreement on 250 pairs with three annotations each. No significance tests reported.

limits: Verifiability is not factuality: the study does not check whether statements are true (authors).
Sentence-level claims only; sentences can hold several claims and citation scope is ambiguous (authors).
Each query-response pair annotated once; agreement measured only on a 250-pair sample.
Systems have different abstention rates (NeevaAI 22.7%), so comparison is hard; no significance tests; correlations rest on four systems.
Closed commercial systems scraped Feb-Mar 2023; results have dated and the internals (model, retriever, decoding) are unknown. ChatGPT and Bard not evaluated for lack of citations.
Copying explanation for the precision-utility trade-off is a hypothesis supported by correlation, not tested causally.

terms.definition: each generated statement about the external world should be fully supported by a set of in-line citations, and each provided citation should support its associated statement
the proportion of verification-worthy statements that are fully supported by their associated citations
